facts: The research article titled "Large Language Models Meet NLP: A Survey" was published in 2025.
The article was published in Frontiers in Computer Science.
The authors of the article include Libo Qin and Philip S. Yu.
The article spans pages 1 to 35.
This study investigates the application of large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT in Natural Language Processing (NLP).
The research introduces a unified taxonomy categorizing LLMs into parameter-frozen and parameter-tuning paradigms.
The study addresses key questions about the resolution of traditional NLP tasks.
It aims to inspire further advancements in the field of NLP.
Large language models (LLMs) are applied in natural language processing (NLP) tasks such as mathematical reasoning and sentiment analysis.
Notable LLMs include the GPT-series, PaLM-series, OPT, and LLaMA.
The paper introduces a new taxonomy categorizing LLM approaches into parameter-frozen and parameter-tuning paradigms.
The research discusses emerging areas and challenges in LLMs for natural language processing.
The section discusses two paradigms: the parameter-frozen paradigm and the parameter-tuning paradigm.
The parameter-frozen paradigm is detailed in section 2.1.
The parameter-tuning paradigm is detailed in section 2.2.
Figure 2 illustrates the two paradigms.
The parameter-frozen paradigm enables prompting in NLP tasks without parameter tuning.
Zero-shot learning uses instruction-following abilities of large language models to perform tasks.
Few-shot learning involves in-context learning by mimicking a limited number of demonstrations.
In few-shot learning, the prompt is formally expressed as P = Prompt(E, I).
Full-parameter tuning involves fine-tuning all model parameters on a training dataset.
Parameter-efficient tuning adjusts a subset of existing parameters or adds new tunable parameters.
Zero-shot learning has the lowest resource consumption and best out-of-domain generalization.
Full-parameter tuning incurs the highest costs but offers the best in-domain performance.
Zero-shot learning is noted for its high application efficiency.
Few-shot learning requires more computational resources than zero-shot learning.
Full-parameter tuning achieves the best in-domain performance with sufficient training data.
Parameter-efficient tuning can match or exceed full-parameter tuning performance in some cases.

Dialogue Understanding is discussed in section 3.3.

Sentiment analysis focuses on identifying the emotional tone of text.
The parameter-frozen paradigm employs zero-shot learning for sentiment classification.
Few-shot learning improves performance by incorporating exemplars.
LoRA is a technique used to enhance LLMs for emotional systems in multi-turn conversations.
Recent studies have explored zero-shot prompting methods leveraging large language models for information extraction.
Siepmann et al. demonstrated the effectiveness of GPT-4 in extracting medical information from discharge letters.
Gu et al. evaluated LLMs for extracting social determinants of health from clinical notes.
Li and Zhang proposed few-shot learning approaches that reformulate information extraction tasks as code.
Dialogue understanding includes spoken language understanding (SLU) and dialogue state tracking (DST).
Zero-shot prompting strategies enhance understanding through step-by-step reasoning.
Few-shot learning has been studied by researchers like Hu et al. and King and Flanigan.
Full-parameter tuning shows significant improvements in dialogue tasks, as demonstrated by Xie et al. and Gupta et al.
Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have enhanced capabilities in zero-shot and few-shot learning.
Researchers Ye et al. and Sui et al. focus on segmenting large tables in the zero-shot learning paradigm.
Luo et al.'s hybrid prompt strategy and Cheng et al.'s Binder redefine table tasks as coding challenges in few-shot learning.
Parameter-efficient tuning methods like LoRA and TableLoRA enhance performance on structured data with minimal adjustments.
Large Language Models (LLMs) are used for classification tasks in Natural Language Generation (NLG).
Summarization is one of the tasks discussed in relation to LLMs.
Code Generation is another task focused on in the section.
Machine Translation is also a task highlighted in the discussion of LLMs.
Zero-shot learning with large language models like GPT-3 shows superior performance in generating concise summaries.
Few-shot learning techniques enhance extractive summarization through in-context learning and dialog-like approaches.
The parameter-tuning paradigm includes full-parameter tuning and parameter-efficient tuning (PET).
Novel strategies like DIONYSUS and Socratic Pretraining optimize LLMs for specific tasks.
Code generation automates the creation of executable code from natural language specifications.
Recent advancements in code generation have been driven by large language models like CodeLLMs and CodeT5+.
Few-shot learning enables models to produce accurate code snippets from minimal examples.
Parameter-efficient tuning methods, such as adapters and LoRA, are competitive in tasks like unit test generation.
Machine translation (MT) uses computers to automatically translate text between languages.
Researchers Zhu et al. and Wei et al. enhance LLMs' multilingual capabilities through instruction-tuning.
OpenBA demonstrates strong performance in Chinese tasks.
Full-parameter tuning methods by Iyer et al. and Feng et al. improve translation accuracy and context-awareness.
Mathematical reasoning in natural language processing utilizes NLP techniques to interpret mathematical texts.
Kojima et al.'s zero-shot chain-of-thought enhances LLMs' reasoning by breaking down problems into manageable steps.
Wei et al.'s chain-of-thought prompting improves reasoning through example selection.
ToolFormer is a technique used in full-parameter tuning to enhance LLMs.

Multilingual LLMs aim to extend English-centric NLP models to over 7,000 languages.
Researchers are exploring multilingual pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning.
A key challenge is improving performance in low-resource languages.
Effective cross-lingual alignment between English and other languages is essential for cross-lingual NLP tasks.
Multi-modal LLMs are being developed to enhance performance in natural language processing (NLP).
Current challenges in multi-modal LLMs include addressing complex multi-modal reasoning.
Most existing models focus on simpler tasks like recognition.
Research is needed to create more effective interaction mechanisms for multi-modal LLMs in NLP applications.
LLMs have shown success in natural language processing (NLP) tasks.
Research is focusing on using LLMs as central controllers for practical NLP tasks.
Current approaches often overlook the selection of suitable tools for LLMs.
Coordinated tool chains are needed for task-oriented dialogue scenarios involving travel bookings.
X-of-thought (XoT) is an approach used in large language models (LLMs).
XoT aims to enhance the ability of LLMs to tackle complex natural language processing tasks.
A key challenge in implementing XoT is developing a universal method for step decomposition.
XoT seeks to effectively integrate diverse prompting knowledge to improve model performance.
Large Language Models (LLMs) can produce outputs that diverge from established world knowledge.
Hallucinations in LLMs undermine their reliability in practical applications.
Developing efficient evaluation benchmarks for hallucinations is a key challenge in NLP.
Exploring how to harness hallucinations can enhance creativity in LLMs.
The application of large language models (LLMs) to downstream NLP tasks raises safety concerns.
Key challenges include the lack of effective safety benchmarks for LLMs.
There are heightened safety risks associated with multilingual contexts.
Research is increasingly focused on ensuring LLM safety for various NLP applications.
Long Chain-of-Thought (Long-CoT) enhances standard Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting.
Long-CoT enables large language models to engage in deeper reasoning.
Key challenges of Long-CoT include adaptive reasoning length control.
Long-CoT incorporates innovations such as reflective mechanisms and reinforcement-learning enhancements.
The work introduces a unified taxonomy that differentiates between parameter-frozen and parameter-tuning paradigms.
The authors received grants from the National Natural Science Foundation of China.
The research spans from 2022 to 2025.
Notable contributions include innovative models such as "Diaggpt," "Cabinet," TableGPT, and Codet5.
